new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work is listed, so the two-work spot-check could not be met; instead I checked the part of this work the compiler did not text-search. I extracted the map pages (pp. 321-2479, 2158 pages, scanned text with 1,238 Stimson notes, logged) and searched for stress / tonique / accentu / prosod / penult / avant-derni / syllab: zero hits. The end-matter index entry 'stress (put the ~ on) 6.8.2.6-1' ( line 2322) is the semantic map entry 'insister / insist' (map on printed p. 1199), not phonological stress. Nothing missed: the whole volume is silent on Tuamotuan stress placement.

audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed penultimate) rests on the best and only dedicated phonology of the language, Kuki 1970 PL B-17, which we hold in full; the deciding quotations are present verbatim at the cited pages (68, 69, 71; phrase stress 67-68, p.9). No later grammar, phonology article or instrumental study of Tuamotuan exists in Glottolog, CrossRef or HAL, and the held 2016 French Polynesian curriculum annex independently states penultimate accent. One refinement worth keeping in the record's notes (not a reclassify): Kuki counts vowels/morae (long vowels = VV, so a word-final long vowel carries stress on its first mora), and his domains are bounded by plus junctures so words of more than three vowels carry more than one 'primary' stress, with phrase stress on the last one — the catalog's word-level penult string encodes the position of that last, phrase-stress-bearing primary stress.
